title: Add a provider-neutral mirror adapter and migration report
author: w0F5vYijNonu8kkqLSa_jYY4GIV-Q5HpbxYY525ggm4

events.title: Add a provider-neutral mirror adapter and migration report
events.body:
## Outcome

Import, continuously mirror, and export a hosted repository through one provider-neutral adapter contract while preserving context and reporting every lossy conversion.

## Implementation

- Define adapter capabilities for Git refs, issues, pull requests, reviews, comments, labels, milestones, discussions, documentation snapshots, workflow definitions and checks, releases and assets, and portable social records.
- Implement one-action onboarding from a standard Git URL plus an adapter credential, with resumable cursors and idempotent retries.
- Support two-way ref and collaboration synchronization with origin markers, conflict records, and loop prevention.
- Preserve source identifiers, timestamps, relationships, attachments, and authorship status without impersonating source signatures; sign local importer provenance.
- Produce a signed migration report listing imported, updated, skipped, unsupported, unverifiable, and failed records plus a resilience summary linked to #439 and #466.

## Acceptance criteria

- A repeated import with the same cursor creates no duplicate refs or records.
- Concurrent changes on both sides produce an explicit conflict instead of silent last-write-wins loss.
- Interrupted code, metadata, and asset transfers resume from durable cursors.
- Unsupported source fields are preserved in the report and never presented as migrated.
- The adapter core has no source-provider names or provider-specific branches; adapter fixtures supply all variance.

## Dependencies

Uses #440 for deterministic records, #461 for releases, and #464/#471 for event and check exchange.

## Verification

Round-trip a fixture repository containing every supported record type through an in-process adapter, interrupt each phase, replay it, and compare refs, relationships, provenance, assets, cursors, and the signed report.
